items.title: Intellectual Property Protection of Purely AI-Generated Content: Rethinking Authorship, Inventorship, and the Case for International Standards
items.abstract: The rapid growth of generative and autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) systems has unsettled the traditionally anthropocentric foundations of intellectual property (IP) law. This article examines the extent to which existing intellectual property rights (IPR) frameworks, namely copyright, patent, and industrial design law, can accommodate works, inventions, and designs that are created exclusively by AI systems without direct human intervention. Adopting a doctrinal legal research methodology, the article reviews primary legal materials, including statutes, international conventions, and case law from several jurisdictions, alongside secondary scholarly literature, to assess how the requirements of authorship, inventorship, originality, and moral rights have been interpreted in the context of purely AI-generated content. The discussion is reinforced by a comparative analysis of jurisdictional responses in the United Kingdom, the European Union, the United States, Australia, South Africa, Indonesia, Hong Kong, China, and the United Arab Emirates. The central argument advanced is that traditional IPR laws were designed around human creativity and therefore struggle to extend coverage to autonomously generated content. While a few jurisdictions have experimented with liberal judicial interpretation or sui generis protection, these efforts remain fragmented, inconsistent, and largely reactive rather than systematic. The article concludes that an internationally coordinated framework, whether through reform of existing treaties or the negotiation of a dedicated IP-AI instrument, is necessary to balance innovation incentives, economic interests, and the public interest in access to AI-generated content.

items.title: INTELLIGENT INFORMATION SYSTEMS FOR EDUCATIONAL MANAGEMENT: A FRAMEWORK FOR DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-MAKING IN NIGERIAN COLLEGES OF EDUCATION
items.abstract: The increasing volume of digital information generated by Colleges of Education creates opportunities for evidence-based educational management, yet institutional data are often distributed across separate administrative systems and are not adequately transformed into actionable intelligence. This study developed an Intelligent Information Systems (IIS) framework for data-driven decision-making in Nigerian Colleges of Education. The study adopted a Design Science Research (DSR) approach, focusing on the identification of the educational-management problem, definition of system requirements, framework design, conceptual demonstration and evaluation. The proposed framework integrates institutional data sources, data integration and quality management, an institutional data repository, Business Intelligence and analytics, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, decision-support mechanisms, management dashboards, and governance, security and human oversight. The framework demonstrates how data relating to students, academic programmes, examinations, personnel, institutional resources and other administrative functions can be transformed from operational records into information and intelligent insights for management decisions. The study argues that integrating heterogeneous institutional data with appropriate analytical and intelligent technologies can strengthen evidence-based planning, monitoring, resource allocation, academic administration and institutional performance management. The framework also emphasises that Artificial Intelligence should complement rather than replace professional judgement, with privacy, security, data quality, transparency and human oversight incorporated into institutional implementation. The study contributes a Computer Science-oriented framework for addressing educational-management information challenges in Nigerian Colleges of Education and provides a conceptual foundation for subsequent prototype development and empirical evaluation.

items.title: Intelligent Systems for Space Conditioning and Shading in Buildings: A Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence Techniques and Their Energy Impact
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) control, whereas solar-radiation management still relies mainly on reactive strategies; whether AI capabilities validated in HVAC could be transferred to solar control has not been systematically assessed. This review compares both domains in terms of experimental maturity, climatic coverage, and input variables. Web of Science studies (2015–2026) reporting quantitative energy-demand variations were systematically reviewed following PRISMA 2020 and synthesized descriptively, with a sensitivity search adding reinforcement-learning and predictive-control terms. Fifty-six studies were included (29 HVAC, 28 solar, 1 shared). HVAC reductions ranged from 3.8% to 62.4% (median 22.1%), a spread associated more with heterogeneous baselines, durations, and metrics than with techniques. Real-world studies represented 31% in HVAC versus 14% in solar management, where AI-based predictive control appeared in one real-world study. Anticipatory variables were scarce but coincided with some of the highest savings, a non-causal association. Model-level patterns, such as Random Forest replication, were not preserved when 18 additional studies were considered. Transferring predictive control from HVAC to solar management is a promising line that requires long-term real-world validation in underrepresented climates. Limitations include a single database and single-reviewer screening. The review was not registered or externally funded.

items.title: INTERACTIVE METHODS FOR DEVELOPING READING COMPREHENSION SKILLS IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE LESSONS
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of reading comprehension skills is an essential component of effective English language teaching, as it enables learners to understand textual information, identify main ideas, interpret contextual meanings, and critically evaluate the information presented. This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of using interactive methods to develop reading comprehension skills in English language lessons. Particular attention is given to reciprocal teaching, jigsaw reading, think-pair-share, problem-based reading, guided questioning, and collaborative text analysis. The study draws on established approaches to reading instruction and research on interactive learning to explain how these methods can facilitate cognitive engagement, metacognitive awareness, learner autonomy, and communicative competence. items.title: IoT and AI-Based Approaches for Monitoring and Preventing Hazards from Inflammable Materials
items.abstract: Inflammable materials pose significant risks in industrial, residential, and transportation environments, often leading to catastrophic fire accidents and economic losses. Traditional hazard detection and safety management systems rely on manual monitoring or delayed response mechanisms, which limit their effectiveness. This research proposes an integrated approach using the Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) for real-time monitoring, prediction, and prevention of hazards related to inflammable materials. IoT-based sensor networks were deployed to continuously track temperature, gas concentration, and environmental parameters, while AI algorithms analyzed the data to identify early warning signs of ignition risks. A hybrid machine learning model combining Support Vector Machines and Deep Neural Networks achieved high accuracy in hazard prediction, significantly reducing false alarms. Experimental simulations demonstrated that the proposed system improves response time and enhances overall safety. The findings suggest that the integration of IoT and AI can serve as a scalable, cost-effective solution for proactive fire prevention and risk management in industries handling inflammable substances.

items.title: IoT-Based Automatic Cotton Leaf Disease Detection, Infection Percentage Estimation, and Treatment Recommendation Using Raspberry PI
items.abstract: Cotton is one of the most important commercial crops worldwide, and its productivity is significantly affected by various leaf diseases such as bacterial blight, alter aria leaf spot, Cercospora leaf spot, powdery mildew, and leaf curl disease. Early and accurate identification of these diseases is essential to minimize crop losses and improve yield. Traditional disease diagnosis relies on manual field inspection by experts, which is time-consuming, labour-intensive, and often impractical for large agricultural fields. The proposed system integrates a Raspberry Pi5, a high-resolution camera module, environmental sensors, and wireless communication technologies to create an intelligent crop monitoring platform. Images of cotton leaves are captured using the Raspberry Pi camera and processed through computer vision techniques for leaf segmentation and feature extraction. A lightweight deep learning model based on MobileNetV2 is employed to automatically identify different cotton leaf diseases. In addition to disease classification, image segmentation techniques are used to calculate the percentage of infected leaf area, enabling the system to determine the severity level of infection. The system also collects environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and light intensity using IoT sensors. These parameters, along with disease diagnosis results, are transmitted to a cloud-based dashboard for real-time monitoring and analysis. Automated alerts can be sent to farmers through SMS or mobile notifications when severe infections are detected. Experimental evaluation is expected to achieve disease classification accuracy above 93%, infection area estimation error below 5%, and real-time inference within one second per image on the Raspberry Pi platform. The proposed solution offers a cost-effective, portable, and scalable approach for precision agriculture by combining artificial intelligence, image processing, and IoT technologies. The system enables early disease detection, accurate infection assessment, timely treatment recommendations, reduced pesticide usage, and improved cotton crop productivity, making it a valuable tool for smart farming applications.

items.title: Iterate on an LLM, Serve on an SLM
items.abstract: As frontier LLMs gain more capabilities, the cost to run them also goes up. At the same time, small language models (SLMs) also gain more capabilities but have largely been able to keep their cost stable, offering 5-40 times cheaper inference for the narrow, repetitive subtasks that agents decompose work into. However, the standing limiting factor is getting the correct behavior out of a small model in a fast, efficient, and economical way. Unfortunately, in most cases, zero-shot small models fail narrow production tasks. Furthermore, retraining one every time the behavior changes is too slow to iterate on. We propose doing both in sequence. First, develop the desired behavior in prompt space, on a frontier model, with immediate feedback from live traffic. Then, once the behavior converges, distill the recorded production behavior (not synthetic imitations of it) into an SLM through supervised fine-tuning (SFT). We show a proper use case of this method through a scheduling agent for home-care agencies that fans out a single yes/no safety decision per caregiver-shift pair on GPT-5.4-nano. A LoRA-tuned Qwen3-8B trained on 11.6k recorded production decisions reaches 0.913 agreement, while the teacher (GPT-5.4-nano), re-run on its own recorded prompts, agrees with itself only 72.7% of the time, pointing to the fact that the SLM may also be more consistent. Furthermore, when the two disagreed, a blinded professional scheduler sided with the student 48-29. Finally, we find that the SLM has approximately 2.5 times lower median latency and is a fraction of the cost. We believe this lifecycle of quick building, live feedback, and cheap inference is a blueprint for others building similar systems.

items.title: KedgeFlow: A Programmable Control Plane for Enterprise AI Agents
items.abstract: Enterprise AI agents can execute altered versions of approved actions, concurrently reuse the same permission, or retry operations whose responses were lost. These failures arise when approval and resource execution lack a shared contract. KedgeFlow specifies language-independent contracts for trusted controllers to authorize state-changing operations and privileged gateways to enforce that authority independently of agent reasoning. Inspired by OpenFlow, it connects policy checks supported by evidence, signed permission for an exact action, a shared allowance that can be consumed only once, target-side conditions for applying the change, and retained outcome records. Under trusted issuance of exact-action authority, two conditional properties establish at most one successful claim per allowance and link every governed dispatch to a matching grant, claim, and subsequent dispatch authorization, even when the agent is compromised. A reference implementation exposes this execution path to agent systems through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In the single-resource evaluation, 6,560 concurrent ledger claim attempts yielded exactly one successful claim for each of 82 allowances. Boundary tests rejected unauthorized and altered requests before consumption. A 32-call gateway race produced one committed mock effect, and a retry after a lost response produced no additional dispatch. Deliberately permissive policy nevertheless authorized an undesirable effect, exposing the limits of execution authorization. Evaluation uses three members of the etcd coordinated key-value store on one host, synthetic authentication and authorization inputs, and a mock target that rejects stale requests. Distributed reservations, enforcement of every production access route, native crash recovery, exactly-once effects at real targets, and interoperability between independent implementations remain untested.

items.title: Knowledge Evolution and Paradigm-Level Change in AI-in-Education Research: A Scientometric Mapping and Critical Review (2015–2025)
items.abstract: Bibliometric commentary increasingly frames the rise of generative artificial intelligence (AI) as a paradigm shift in AI-in-education (AIED) research, yet rarely distinguishes publication growth from genuine reconfiguration of the knowledge base or of teacher–learner roles. This study maps knowledge evolution in AIED from 2015 to 2025 by integrating four analytical strands across Web of Science and Scopus: scientometric mapping (including keyword and reference bursts and co-citation analysis), structural topic modeling (STM), design-weighted coding of full texts, and triangulation across these strands. Two transition windows emerged. The weaker 2019–2020 window (Jensen–Shannon divergence, JSD = 0.058; retained under the permutation rule but not under a stricter interval-based rule) reflects a research-front transition toward learning analytics and prediction, accompanied by knowledge-base reconfiguration but no detectable change in teacher–learner roles. The 2022–2023 window (JSD = 0.187, the period maximum) coincides with the generative-AI surge and couples a newly formed co-citation community with a topic-specific rise in coagency whose direction is clear but whose magnitude is imprecisely estimated. Because these effects concentrate in 36.6% of the weighted corpus and recent citations remain right-censored, we classify the change, under our pre-specified labeling scheme, as localized paradigm-level reconfiguration rather than a field-level paradigm shift. The label is an operational classification within that scheme, not an independent determination that a paradigm shift has occurred.

items.title: Knowledge generation and evaluation for construction quality assessment using retrieval-augmented large language models
items.abstract: To address the problems of delayed knowledge updating, inefficient information acquisition, and difficulty in cross-project knowledge reuse in civil engineering construction quality assessment, this paper proposes a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based methodology for injecting domain knowledge into large language models (LLMs). Multi-source knowledge, including national standards, journal articles, textbooks, and engineering reports, was systematically collected, cleaned, semantically segmented, and encoded using the bge-large-zh-v1.5 model to build a Milvus vector database. A general-purpose LLM was selected via semantic perplexity, and similarity-based retrieval was employed to construct prompt templates integrating role settings, prior knowledge, user queries, and response requirements, thereby enabling domain adaptation without additional training. An evaluation dataset containing 390 objective questions from registered architect and supervising engineer qualification examinations was constructed, and six representative LLMs along with their RAG-enhanced counterparts were evaluated. The results show that the average accuracy of general LLMs is 61.3%, with DeepSeek achieving the highest at 73.9%; after RAG enhancement, the accuracy rises to 86.3%, with significant improvements across all subjects. The proposed method effectively mitigates the hallucination phenomenon and provides traceable answers with source citations, enhancing both professionalism and interpretability, and offering a viable technical pathway for the digital transformation of the civil engineering industry.

items.title: Large Language Models (LLMs) as Peer Reviewers: A Comparative Study with Human Reviewers of Manuscripts in Pediatric Dentistry
items.abstract: The peer review process plays a fundamental role in evaluating the quality of scientific manuscripts, but it can be subject to challenges related to time, variability among reviewers, and the subjectivity of evaluations. With the advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini have been proposed as potential resources to support the evaluation of scientific manuscripts. This study aims to analyze and compare the quality of the reviews produced by these LLMs with those prepared by human reviewers in the evaluation of manuscripts in Pediatric Dentistry. A comparative study will be conducted using scientific manuscripts published under an open peer review policy in the journals BMJ Open, PeerJ, and F1000Research. Primary studies of different designs and systematic reviews will be included, using the initial submission versions of the manuscripts and the respective complete reviews from human reviewers referring to the first round of editorial evaluation. Manuscripts will be submitted in their entirety to the ChatGPT (GPT-4o), Claude (3.5 Sonnet), and Gemini (1.5 Pro) models, using a standardized master prompt adapted only for the study design. Human reviews and those produced by LLMs will be anonymized, structurally standardized, and blinded to their origin. Two independent reviewers, previously trained and calibrated, will assess the reviews for overall quality using a structured instrument, for themes and critical patterns using hybrid thematic analysis, and for thematic diversity using the Shannon Diversity Index. The variation in review quality according to the study design will also be explored. The overall quality of the reviews will be considered the primary outcome. Statistical analyses will be performed using linear mixed-effects models to compare quality scores and thematic diversity, and logistic regression mixed-effects models to analyze the identified themes, considering the paired structure of the reviews linked to each manuscript. This study is expected to contribute to expanding knowledge about the potential and limitations of LLMs in peer review in Pediatric Dentistry, providing evidence for future research on their use as a tool to support the critical evaluation of scientific manuscripts.

items.title: Large Language Models for Intelligent Data Engineering: Automating Schema Design, Lineage, and Quality Control
items.abstract: This research investigates the application of large language models (LLMs) to automate key data engineering tasks, including schema design, data lineage tracking, and quality control. It presents an integrated framework combining language models with traditional data engineering tools to improve productivity while maintaining accuracy and reliability. The paper explores automated schema generation from business requirements, lineage extraction from SQL queries and ETL scripts, and AI-enhanced data quality monitoring. It also discusses validation techniques, human-in-the-loop review, prompt engineering, error handling, and integration with existing engineering workflows. The study reports potential reductions of approximately 70% in schema design time, improvements of over 80% in lineage documentation completeness, and a 65% acceleration in quality issue detection. It also addresses limitations such as hallucinations, inconsistent outputs, context-window constraints, and privacy risks. This work provides practical guidance for organizations adopting LLM-based data engineering automation while retaining essential human oversight and production validation. items.title: LEVERAGING ICT AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN STUDENT RECORDS MANAGEMENT IN NIGERIAN UNIVERSITIES
items.abstract: This study focuses on the role of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in student records management in Nigerian Universities. Student records are critical to the admission and registration process, to course enrolment, for the processing of examinations, to academic progression and graduation, to the production of student transcripts, to institutional decision making, and beyond. But in a lot of Nigerian universities, records retrieval, storage of files, loss of files, duplication of records, inaccurate data entry, lack of reliable electronic system of access etc., continue to plague many universities in Nigeria. A qualitative Integrative Review Method was used in the study, which involved a literature review on relevant research on the use of ICT in electronic records management, education management information systems and emerging applications of AI in higher education. The review demonstrates how ICT tools such as databases, student-information systems, online portals, cloud storage, scanning technologies and electronic document-management tools can enhance the rapidity, accuracy, security and accessibility of student records as well as their preservation. AI can also assist with intelligent document classification, optical character recognition, duplicate-record detection, automated enquiries, and anomaly identification and predictive academic analysis. However, these technologies are currently limited by low levels of funding, unreliable electricity, poor internet connectivity, dated equipment, lack of employee training, low levels of interoperability, and a lack of organizational readiness or concerns about cybersecurity. The study also found that it is not just a matter of providing hardware and software to enable successful technology-driven records management. It requires institutional commitment, skilled personnel, reliable infrastructure, data-governance policies, interoperability, regular maintenance, cybersecurity safeguards and compliance with data-protection requirements. The paper makes a number of recommendations, including the creation of integrated student-information systems, ongoing training for registry and ICT staff, the implementation of unique student identifiers, the systematic digitisation of paper records, and the careful and supervised use of AI.

items.title: Limitations on Autoregressive Token Generation via Sequential Sampling
items.abstract: We study autoregressive token generation through the notion of sequential samplers: A circuit that samples the next symbol only given the previous ones and possibly a small amount of state. We show that (1) a sequential sampler with $k$ bits of state can be simulated by a stateless one at a roughly $O(2^{k})$ size overhead; (2) efficient insertional sampling (Stern, Chan, Kiros, Uszkoreit, ICML 2019) is more powerful than efficient sequential sampling in any fixed order; (3) sequential samplers with small state cannot establish certain forms of covert cryptographic channels. Result (1), together with the pseudoentropy vs. sequential sampleability duality of Vadhan and Zheng (STOC 2012), characterizes efficient sequential sampleability with small state. Result (3) provides a potential safety mechanism against subliminal coordination among malicious LLM agents.

items.title: LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising
items.abstract: Dynamic Product Advertising (DPA) retrieval systems are a core component of modern e-commerce advertising; however, their evaluation remains challenging. Conventional offline engagement metrics are limited by sparse, biased feedback, while online evaluation is costly and time-consuming. In this work, we propose a user--product relevance metric for offline evaluation of DPA retrieval systems. The metric first compresses the engagement history into a compact set of intent representatives via Semantic-ID-grouped, event-stratified segmentation, then assesses the relevance of a recommended product to each individual intent and aggregates them as a user-level relevance score, yielding a stable and interpretable measure of retrieval quality. To compute this metric at scale, we leverage large language models (LLMs) as semantic relevance judges, capturing nuanced functional and semantic relationships that heuristic methods often miss. We propose an agentic, human-aligned prompting framework that generates multi-category relevance guidelines and distills teacher-model judgments into an efficient student model for scalable evaluation. The resulting metric strongly correlates with offline and online business metrics, enabling faster and more reliable DPA retrieval iteration before A/B testing.

items.title: Local Culture, History, and Languages in Curriculum Content and Student Engagement in Liberia: A Case Study of Margibi and Bong County School Systems
items.abstract: Abstract This study investigates how integrating local culture, history, and indigenous languages into the national curriculum enhances student engagement in Liberian schools, focusing specifically on the Margibi and Bong County school systems. Historically, post-conflict educational frameworks in Liberia have relied on imported or legacy academic models, which can alienate students from their lived realities and diminish classroom participation. This paper examines the role of culturally responsive pedagogy in bridging the gap between formal schooling and indigenous heritage. Utilizing a mixed-methods research design incorporating surveys, classroom observations, and key informant interviews with teachers and administrators in Kakata, Suakoko, and surrounding districts, the study evaluates behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement outcomes. The findings demonstrate that embedding local historical narratives, community-based traditions, and indigenous linguistic elements significantly improves student motivation, retention, and academic performance. The paper concludes with actionable recommendations for the Ministry of Education and local school districts to advance context-driven curriculum reforms.

items.title: Long Working Hours and the Co-Occurrence of Work-Related Musculoskeletal Symptoms and Occupational Stress among Ride-Hailing Drivers in Beijing, China
items.abstract: Long working hours may be associated with adverse health outcomes among ride-hailing drivers. The study aims to examine the associations between long working hours, work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) and occupational stress. Additionally, it explores the association between long working hours and the co-occurrence of WMSDs and occupational stress. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 668 ride-hailing drivers in Beijing, China, from August to October 2024. WMSDs were assessed using the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ). Occupational stress was assessed using the Job Content Questionnaire (JCQ). In this study, co-occurrence was defined as the joint classification of WMSDs and occupational stress in the same individual. Participants were categorized into groups of <55 and ≥55 working hours per week. Binary and logistic regression models were used to examine the associations between weekly working hours and health outcomes. Overall, 77.8% of participants worked ≥55 h per week. The prevalence of WMSDs and occupational stress was 53.0% and 56.4%, respectively. Weekly working hours ≥55 h were significantly associated with higher odds of occupational stress after full adjustment (aOR = 3.99, 95% CI: 2.59–6.13), but were not significantly associated with WMSDs (aOR = 1.12, 95% CI: 0.74–1.70). Occupational stress was associated with higher odds of WMSDs (aOR = 1.56, 95% CI: 1.11–2.18). Compared with drivers working <55 h per week, those working ≥55 h per week had higher odds of having one condition (aOR = 1.95, 95% CI: 1.21–3.14) and co-occurrence of occupational stress and WMSDs (aOR = 4.64, 95% CI: 2.57–8.36). The prevalence of co-occurrence was 37.9% in the ≥55 h group and 16.2% in the <55 h group. Long working hours were associated with occupational stress and with the co-occurrence of occupational stress and WMSDs among ride-hailing drivers. However, no independent association was observed between long working hours and WMSDs. These findings highlight the need for comprehensive occupational health interventions targeting ride-hailing drivers.

items.title: Lumen-bench: Cross-Lingual Safety Gaps and the Say-Do Problem in Tool-Calling Large Language Models
items.abstract: When a large language model refuses an unethical request, what does refusal mean? In conversation, refusal is bounded by what the model says; once the model is equipped with executable tools, what it does can diverge from what it says, a failure mode that English-only evaluations cannot fully reveal. We introduce Lumen-bench, a behavioral benchmark of tool-calling ethics spanning 30 models, five languages (Portuguese, English, Spanish, Mandarin Chinese, Hindi), 108 Portuguese-authored scenarios, six social-pressure conditions, two system prompts (ethical and neutral), and 21 generic tools. The evaluation comprises 194,400 trials. Judgments come from a reasoning-model judge (o4-mini), calibrated against one Portuguese-speaking author ($n=83$; harmful/non-harmful $κ=0.78$), compared with two other provider judges (Fleiss' $κ=0.78$, $n=607$), and complemented by retrospective sandbox replay. Four findings emerge. (i) Within-model comparisons support higher harmful-action rates in Hindi and Portuguese than English under the ethical prompt, and Hindi and Spanish under the neutral prompt, after multiple-testing correction. (ii) Premium models have lower median violation rates, although price does not guarantee safety or competence. (iii) Replacing the ethical system prompt with a neutral one raises pooled violation rates from 2.76\% to 13.64\%. (iv) In 8.57\% of substantive-call cases, refusal or ethical objection accompanies a harmful tool call: the judges consistently identify the say-do gap, although they differ in how many responses they assign to this category. Matched benign controls demonstrate legitimate task completion in 82.8\% of 3,300 trials. Code and reproduction scripts are available at https://github.com/TropicAI-Research/lumen.

items.title: Malware Detection with Autonomous Agents: A Review of Functional Roles, Datasets, and Coordination Readiness
items.abstract: Large language models are increasingly written into malware detection systems, yet the literature reports them under a single label that obscures what they actually do, and existing surveys either treat agents in the abstract or malware detection without them. This review closes that gap. It is the first to examine the implemented strand of agent-based malware detection as a coordinated system rather than a catalogue of techniques, and to ask how well positioned the field is to support multi-agent operation. We make three contributions. First, we introduce a functional classification that groups each system by which of four roles the model fills, namely perception, reasoning and decision-making, adaptive monitoring, and collaborative learning, treating the mature body of standalone detectors as the foundation rather than the object of review. Second, from a corpus of recent primary studies we derive a modality-based dataset taxonomy, a map linking datasets to the role the model plays, and a pipeline-stage and role-coverage matrix for the agent-based systems. Third, we assess which existing detectors are structurally ready for agentisation and why. The analysis yields three findings. What varies across the field is not which model is used but where in the detection chain it sits. Role coverage is bimodal, with perception and reasoning served almost everywhere while adaptive monitoring is realised by a single system in the corpus and collaborative learning by none. And uniformly high reported accuracy reflects curated, single-split evaluation rather than robustness. Reading these together, the discriminating property for agentisation is whether a system exposes anything between input and verdict, which makes integration and orchestration, not the invention of new detectors, the principal open problem.

items.title: Mapping of Musculoskeletal Complaints Among Maintenance Technicians Using the Nordic Body Map at PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa Tbk
items.abstract: This study aims to map the location and intensity of subjective musculoskeletal complaints among technicians at Workshop Plant 5 of PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa Tbk using the Nordic Body Map (NBM). A quantitative descriptive approach was applied to questionnaire data collected from five technicians over three working days, covering 28 body regions. Of the 420 responses, 349 (83.10%) indicated no pain, while 71 (16.90%) reported mild pain, with no moderate or severe complaints. Four technicians (80%) reported at least one mild complaint. The highest proportions of mild pain were found in the left and right thighs, knees, and calves, each accounting for 7 of 15 responses (46.67%), followed by the lower neck and back, each with 5 of 15 responses (33.33%), and the left and right shoulders, each with 4 of 15 responses (26.67%). These findings describe the distribution of subjective complaints and help identify priority body regions for further ergonomic evaluation. This study did not assess postural risks, diagnose musculoskeletal disorders, or examine associations between complaints and work activities. Literature-based improvement proposals require further feasibility assessment in the workplace.

items.title: MARL-BattleGrounds: A Novel JAX-native Benchmark for Heterogeneous and Competitive Multi-agent RL
items.abstract: We present MARL-BattleGrounds (MARL-BGs), an easy-to-use JAX-native benchmark for heterogeneous and competitive multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), designed to be sample-efficient, computationally efficient, and researcher-centric. MARL benchmarks are typically simple and efficient, like SMAX, where winning reduces to unit micromanagement, or rich and costly, like Dota 2. MARL-BGs fills this missing middle. Its first mode, Team Deathmatch, is a simultaneous turn-based game between two teams of five heterogeneous agents. The five classes have distinct basic, passive, and ultimate abilities designed to synergize with allies and counter enemies. Our 52 hand-designed maps with diverse obstacles include a 12-map curriculum and ten held-out validation and test maps. MARL-BGs provides two canonical evaluation modes. First, eight endgame scenarios form a hard generalization challenge: each asks a team to win an unseen, nearly lost position against a strong reactive controller within 5-10 ticks. Second, a monthly round-robin tournament retrains each submission on equal compute, plays it against every member of the current "Big Nine" field, and publishes the Elo results on the official leaderboard. All entrants are publicly released as downloadable opponents. MARL-BGs records 11,192 metrics per game in 28 topics. We also include three strong scripted opponents, an analytical replay viewer, and off-the-shelf tools for self-play, cross-play, curriculum learning, and zero-shot coordination evaluation. We even provide an API for LLM-based agents and use it to evaluate Qwen3.5-9B against our strongest policy. In our BattleClient, humans can play alongside or against any mix of policies, enabling human-AI evaluation. We benchmark MARL-BGs with six additional deep MARL baselines, which we release. On one RTX 5090 with 1,024 parallel games, the simulator runs 50,000 5v5 game steps per second.

items.title: Mentors’ Perspectives on Supporting Newly Graduated Registered Nurses in Hospital Settings: A Qualitative Focus Group Study
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Research consistently highlights the importance of mentorship and a supportive work environment for newly graduated registered nurses entering clinical settings. Previous research on mentorship has primarily focused on new nurses' perspectives. Further research is needed to explore mentors' perspectives in greater depth. AIM: To explore mentors' perspectives on supporting newly graduated registered nurses in their professional development in a hospital setting. DESIGN: The study had a qualitative explorative design using focus group discussions as a data collection method. METHOD: A total of 18 registered nurses serving as mentors in a hospital care unit participated in five focus group discussions. The data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. FINDINGS: The findings revealed mentors' views that a permissive approach, creating a trusting relationship, and strengthening self-confidence build a positive foundation for novice nurses. They wished to facilitate novice nurses' learning towards professional independence by encouraging reflection and probing, and by fostering a desire for ongoing clinical competence development and patient safety through their presence in daily practice. CONCLUSION: These findings underscore the crucial role of mentors as advanced nurses in fostering supportive learning environments for newly graduated registered nurses by establishing meaningful mentoring relationships that offer psychological support. The findings of this study may support mentors and nurse managers responsible for facilitating the transition of newly graduated registered nurses into hospital settings by informing mentorship approaches that promote professional development through workplace learning and foster psychological safety during the transition period. items.title: Microplastics and the Kidney: A Narrative Review of Human Evidence, Molecular Mechanisms of Cell Injury, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are widespread environmental contaminants, but their potential effects on kidney health remain poorly defined. As an organ continuously exposed to circulating particles and involved in their urinary elimination, the kidney may represent both a target of MP toxicity and a route of excretion. In this narrative review, we examine current evidence linking MPs to kidney injury, integrating experimental, mechanistic, and human data. Particular attention is given to the early events governing particle–cell interactions. After exposure, micro- and nanoplastics acquire an eco- and biomolecular corona that modifies their surface properties, cellular recognition, uptake, and biodistribution. Following internalization through phagocytic and endocytic pathways, particles may accumulate within endolysosomal compartments and interact with intracellular structures, disrupting cellular homeostasis. In renal cells, these events converge on mitochondrial dysfunction, reactive oxygen species generation, endoplasmic reticulum stress, inflammatory signaling, altered autophagy, and regulated cell death. Several interconnected pathways have been implicated, including Keap1–Nrf2/ARE and NF-κB signaling, MAPK and IRE1/XBP1-mediated stress responses, ACSL4–GPX4-related ferroptosis, and TGF-β1-related profibrotic signaling. Human studies have detected MPs in urine and kidney tissue and provide preliminary evidence linking MP burden with early markers of kidney damage, although current findings remain limited by small study populations and substantial methodological heterogeneity. Patients with chronic kidney disease, particularly those receiving dialysis, may represent a population of special interest because potentially altered renal handling may coexist with repeated exposure to polymer-based medical devices and dialysis fluids. Despite this potential relevance, data on MP exposure and accumulation in CKD and dialysis patients remain remarkably scarce. We finally discuss the limitations of current experimental models and analytical methods and the need for standardized biomonitoring, more environmentally relevant particles and exposure concentrations, and detection strategies capable of reaching the nanoscale, including artificial intelligence-assisted analysis. Overall, available evidence provides a mechanistic basis for MP-induced kidney injury, but its clinical relevance and contribution to human kidney disease remain to be established.

items.abstract: Recent advances in articial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models, havesignicantly improved performance in language understanding, vision, and reasoning. How-ever, a fundamental limitation remains: current AI systems still lack an explicit under-standing of the logical structure by which humans make decisions within specic situationsand relationships. This limitation is not merely a shortage of intelligence, but a missinglayer of context-dependent decision logic. This study proposes a theoretical framework andmethodological protocol that redenes human cooperation as an observable information owrather than a psychological or moral phenomenon. We model cooperative propagation asRipple structures, which are directional causal chains of actions in which A helps B and B inturn helps C, and we introduce the concept of a Behavioral Digital Twin, dened as a map-ping of decision logic derived from situation, relationships, and action history. We furtherpresent a non-interventional observational protocol for capturing naturally occurring coop-erative behaviors through naturalistic observation environments, and outline a validationframework for future empirical work. All behavioral events remain voluntary; the proto-col introduces observation infrastructure without prescribing or incentivizing actions. Allgures and examples in this manuscript are conceptual illustrations intended to clarify the-oretical constructs. This work aims to provide a foundational layer connecting AI research,social systems research, and Web3 governance.

items.title: More Domains, No Gains? FLO: Fast-Slow Reciprocal Learning for Multi-Domain Graph Pre-training
items.abstract: Inspired by the great success of foundation models in the development of artificial general intelligence, Graph Foundation Models (GFMs) have recently attracted significant attention and have the potential to advance graph intelligence. Exhibiting such intelligence requires effectively learning knowledge from large-scale, multi-domain graph data during pre-training. Increasing domain diversity during pre-training is expected to yield richer and more generalizable knowledge. Most existing methods pursue this goal by designing domain alignment strategies that help a single graph model learn from multiple domains. However, we observe that existing methods struggle to benefit from increasing domain diversity. Through empirical and theoretical analysis, we reveal two key limitations. Firstly, pre-training in most GFMs is confined to a single message-passing paradigm. Since propagation flattens relations among neighboring nodes, the graph model can hardly perceive the knowledge beyond propagation, namely the attribute-predictable component of these relations. Secondly, domain alignment strategies often rely on randomly initialized parameters that are jointly updated with the graph model using immediate loss feedback, leaving early knowledge acquisition vulnerable to cross-domain interference. To address these issues, we propose FLO, a Fast--sLow reciprOcal approach for multi-domain graph pre-training. Specifically, a propagation-free attribute branch predicts the graph model's relations without message passing and returns these predictions to refine the model. We further stabilize knowledge acquisition by pairing a fast process that adapts to the current domain with a slow process that integrates knowledge across domains. On 12 datasets, FLO benefits from increasing domain diversity and achieves the best average performance in cross-domain and cross-task transfer.

items.title: MoSAIC: Learning DAG Scheduling Heuristics from Optimal Schedules through Motif-Aware Recovery and LLM-Guided Reasoning
items.abstract: Efficient task scheduling in heterogeneous computing systems remains a fundamental challenge in embedded and high-level synthesis flows. This paper presents MoSAIC (Motif-aware Scheduling with AI-driven Cognition), a learning-based framework that bridges the gap between exact and heuristic scheduling approaches for DAG-based applications. The system uses the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to learn the relationships between DAG structures and scheduling priority functions. The framework first leverages the OR-Tools CP-SAT solver [4] to generate optimal schedules, which are then used to supervise the learning of compact priority-based scheduling functions through Bayesian Optimization. These learned heuristics capture relationships between scheduling decisions and structural graph features such as rank, depth, and fanout, enabling the construction of a reusable knowledge base across diverse DAG instances. Experimental results across synthetic graph families and real-world benchmarks, including PolyBench and MachSuite, show that the learned heuristics consistently improve over classical approaches such as HEFT [2], while maintaining low runtime overhead. The results indicate that combining optimal supervision with learning-based generalization provides a practical approach for scalable and adaptive task scheduling.

items.abstract: Teacher work motivation and group dynamics are essential in supporting educational quality. Teachers often face challenges such as heavy workloads, limited facilities, administrative demands, and personal differences that affect motivation, communication, and collaboration. This article explores Sharia-based values as an approach to strengthening teacher motivation and group dynamics in Islamic educational institutions. Using a descriptive qualitative literature review, the study examines recent publications on work motivation, group dynamics, Islamic leadership, and Sharia values. Findings show that values of ikhlas (sincerity), amanah (trustworthiness), ihsan (excellence), ta’awun (mutual assistance), ukhuwah (brotherhood), and syura (consultation) strengthen intrinsic motivation, professional responsibility, mutual support, effective communication, and collaborative relationships among teachers. Islamic leadership plays a key role in translating these values into practice through fairness, exemplary conduct, participation, and open communication. Integrating Sharia values into school management provides a foundation for enhancing professionalism, cooperation, positive group dynamics, and a supportive work environment, ultimately improving educational quality.

items.title: Motivation And Performance In Project-Based Organizations: Evidence From Abia State, Nigeria
items.abstract: This study examined the relationship between motivation and performance in project-based organizations in Abia State, Nigeria.Specifically, it investigated the influence of intrinsic motivation on individual performance; the effect of extrinsic motivational factors on team performance; the mediating roles of knowledge sharing and collaborative behaviors in the motivation-innovation performance relationship; and the moderating role of corporate culture in the motivation-project performance relationship.The study adopted a pragmatist philosophical position and a convergent parallel mixed-methods design.Quantitative data were obtained through a structured questionnaire from 402 valid respondents out of 420 distributed questionnaires, representing a 95.7% response rate, while qualitative evidence was obtained from 22 semi-structured interviews.Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, regression, Hayes PROCESS mediation and moderation procedures, and thematic analysis.Results showed that intrinsic motivation strongly predicted individual performance (β = 0.634, R² = 0.402, p < 0.001), while extrinsic motivation significantly predicted team performance (β = 0.492, R² = 0.242, p < 0.001).Knowledge sharing and collaborative behaviors significantly mediated motivation and innovation performance, with indirect effects of 0.152 and 0.127, respectively.Corporate culture significantly moderated the motivation-project performance relationship (interaction B = 0.192, p < 0.001), with the model explaining 42.0% of variance.The findings indicate that project-based organizations should combine intrinsic and extrinsic motivational practices with supportive cultural conditions and structured knowledge-sharing mechanisms.

items.title: Motivation, work, and mobility: developing a process framework of employee turnover intentions in Indian nonprofits
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the mechanisms associated with employees’ turnover intentions in Indian non-profit organisations (NPOs). Existing employee turnover research provides limited understanding of how individual, organisational, and sector-level dynamics relate to turnover intentions in Indian NPOs. To address this gap, the study aims to develop a process-orientated framework grounded in employees' lived experiences. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted a qualitative approach using semi-structured interviews with 17 non-profit employees, managers, leaders, and sector stakeholders. Participants were purposively selected to capture diverse organisational roles and sector experiences. Data were analysed using the Gioia methodology. Findings The analysis develops a process framework comprising five interconnected dimensions: mission attachment spectrum, employment deal and financial viability, work design and career trajectories, leadership and organisational culture, and development-sector labour-market dynamics. Together, these dimensions describe how employees evaluate their employment conditions, interpret their relationship with the organisational mission, and respond to opportunities in the broader development-sector labour-market. Originality/value This study contributes a process-orientated framework of employee turnover intentions, advancing four theoretical propositions grounded in qualitative evidence from the Indian non-profit sector. The framework extends the employee turnover literature by integrating individual, organisational, and sector-level dynamics into a contextual explanation of employee turnover intentions in Indian NPOs. The framework illustrates how turnover intentions may emerge through the interaction of mission attachment, organisational conditions, and development-sector labour-market dynamics over time. These insights may have relevance not only to Indian NPOs but also to NPOs operating in other resource-constrained and emerging economy contexts.

items.title: Multimodal Trust Assessment in Human–AI Shared Control Systems
items.abstract: Trust plays an important role in human–AI shared-control systems, yet it is difficult to assess from a single observable signal. This study proposes an event-centered multimodal framework for assessing situational trust by integrating contextual, behavioral, affective, and individual features surrounding critical human–AI interaction events. A controlled autonomous-driving experiment was conducted with 15 participants under high- and low-reliability conditions, yielding 117 valid event-level observations with retrospective trust ratings. The results showed substantial differences in reported trust between reliability conditions and across failure types, while facial and failure-related contextual indicators were among the more informative variables. However, the highly imbalanced trust classes, particularly the limited number of high-trust observations, constrained reliable classification of individual trust levels. The findings only provide preliminary evidence that event-level multimodal observations can characterize information associated with reported situational trust, while also demonstrating the challenges of cross-user trust estimation under limited and imbalanced data. Therefore, the study serves as a methodological and empirical starting point for developing more robust multimodal trust assessment approaches, rather than as a validation of a generalized real-time trust prediction system.

items.title: NAVIGATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND RELIGIOUS AUTHORITY IN NIGERIA: RECONFIGURING RELIGIOUS KNOWLEDGE, LEADERSHIP AND TRUST IN THE DIGITAL AGE
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming part of religious education, communication, research and everyday faith practices. Believers can now use generative AI to explain sacred texts, compare interpretations, prepare devotional materials and seek answers to religious questions without first consulting a recognised religious leader. This development raises an important question for Nigeria: how is religious authority changing when access to religious information is no longer controlled mainly by clergy, scholars and religious institutions? This paper examines the relationship between AI and religious authority in Nigeria, focusing on religious knowledge, leadership and trust. Using a conceptual and interpretive methodology, it synthesises scholarship on religious authority, digital religion, AI ethics and Nigerian religious experience. It argues that AI is not simply replacing religious authorities; rather, it is reconfiguring the conditions under which authority is produced, accessed, evaluated and trusted. Nigerian digital-religion research shows that digital infrastructures can create new forms of religious influence and authority, while recent AI scholarship highlights concerns about accuracy, privacy, bias and human accountability. The paper proposes a Responsible Religious AI Engagement Framework based on human accountability, verification, contextual sensitivity, confidentiality and formation. It concludes that Nigerian religious institutions should neither reject AI nor surrender religious judgment to it. AI should remain an assistive instrument while theological discernment, pastoral responsibility, communal recognition and human dignity remain central to religious leadership.

items.title: No, Your Tools Are Not Enough: It's Time to Bring Agents to the Hunt
items.abstract: Modern software systems are large and complex, demanding scalable and autonomous techniques for vulnerability discovery. Existing approaches still depend on human expertise for domain knowledge, and on human intervention throughout the process of vulnerability discovery. AI agents offer us an opportunity to make vulnerability discovery more adaptive, scalable, and autonomous. Agents bring the ability to make continuous decisions and adapt, and general knowledge that can be augmented. In this paper, we present our experience using AI agents to find vulnerabilities across diverse programs such as Windows drivers, the Linux kernel, XNU, firmware, and web applications. We use an iterative agentic workflow and find that it generalizes across these targets. We discuss tasks that agents help with, which were previously challenging, and some future research directions we consider important for advancing autonomous vulnerability discovery.

items.title: Noncommutative Cultural Dynamics: A Unified State-Space Framework for Weakly and Strongly Correlated Cultural Fields
items.abstract: This project develops a unified mathematical and computational framework for cultural dynamics based on noncommutative operators, state-space modeling, and multi-scale correlation structures. Cultural change is represented as the evolution of latent cultural fields that may be weakly correlated (ancient and pre-modern societies) or strongly correlated (modern media-driven environments). The model integrates continuous-time dynamics, discrete noncommutative transitions, generational eigenmodes, and media-induced perturbations. The framework is extended across multiple structural layers: (1) network-based cultural diffusion using graph Laplacians, (2) spatial cultural propagation via partial differential equations, (3) AI-based implementations including neural ODEs, graph neural networks, physics-informed neural networks, and diffusion models, (4) optimal control formulations for policy intervention, (5) evolutionary game-theoretic cultural adaptation, (6) general-equilibrium economic integration, and (7) narrative-field modeling for story generation and cultural feedback. Together, these components form a comprehensive “Unified Cultural Field Theory” that connects cultural sociology, cognitive science, AI theory, narrative studies, economics, and noncommutative geometry. The project situates cultural dynamics within a rigorous mathematical structure while enabling practical applications in media analysis, trend forecasting, policy design, and generative AI.

items.title: Observing passenger behavior and motion sickness development in autonomous vehicles – A driving study on public roads
items.abstract: Highly automated vehicles (HAV) enable passengers to engage in non-driving related activities (NDRA), which are a known factor for increasing motion sickness (MS). Surveys show that NDRAs will not significantly change compared to manual driving, but they lack experiential insight. The study investigated NDRAs in automated versus manual driving, the influence of MS susceptibility, and the effect of self-chosen NDRAs on MS. In the online survey (N = 611), 52% of participants reported avoiding NDRAs to prevent MS. NDRA frequency showed a small but significant effect of MS susceptibility on certain NDRA choices. Within the on-road study (N = 44), most participants (86%) chose reading as NDRA, either on a smartphone or in a book. Video recordings showed smartphones and tablets as the most frequently used devices. No influence of MS susceptibility on NDRA choice was observed in automated driving. Most participants reported they were reading during MS occurrence.

items.title: Optimising Automotive Wiring Harness Production Through Collaborative Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twins: A Structured Narrative Review
items.abstract: Automotive wiring harnesses are safety-critical subassemblies whose complexity grows with driver-assistance systems, electrification, and connectivity, while pre-assembly and final assembly remain predominantly manual. This structured narrative review examines how collaborative robots (cobots), AI-based perception and planning, and Digital Twins (DTs) support harness production, with deformable-linear-object (DLO) perception and manipulation treated as a cross-cutting harness-specific domain. A database search (2015–early 2026) yielded 64 studies; citation tracking and a targeted update to 30 August 2026 added 19, giving an evidence base of 83 studies. Reported outcomes were separated into algorithm, task, operator, and system levels, and maturity was graded with explicit, review-specific Technology Readiness Level (TRL) criteria. Most evidence is at the algorithm, task, or operator level. Harness-specific cobot workstations reach industrially relevant prototype validation for single operations—for example, cobot-assisted taping with an approximately 50% reduction in ergonomic risk scores and a 12% shorter cycle—whereas harness-specific perception and DLO manipulation remain mainly at laboratory level. System-level evidence on throughput, changeover, and cost is scarce, and no continuously operating cell integrating the three core domains was identified. Key gaps concern branched DLO modelling, ergonomics-aware task planning, Human Digital Twins, connector design for automation, DT-supported safety verification, digital continuity, and reconfigurable hardware.

items.title: Optimize Once, Execute Fast: Latency-Aware Multi-Agent Workflow Learning for Recurrent Queries
items.abstract: Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-based MAS) have shown remarkable success in solving complex tasks by coordinating specialized agents through multi-step workflows. To overcome the high cost and specificity of manually designed workflows, recent research has shifted toward learning them automatically. However, a key limitation remains: while agent calls introduce significant latency due to model inference time and service congestion, most automated methods optimize solely for downstream performance, ignoring execution time (makespan). This issue is amplified when workflows are reused across recurring queries, making latency accumulate over time. This limits deployment in recurrent applications such as AI customer support and AI cloud troubleshooting, where users expect fast responses. To bridge this gap, we introduce a new problem, termed latency-aware workflow generation, where the objective is to minimize workflow makespan while aiming to retain downstream performance. We propose LAWA (Latency-Aware Workflow optimizAtion), a novel framework that reduces makespan via theoretically grounded graph edits targeting critical-path bottlenecks. By unifying a graph generator with this graph-editing procedure, LAWA supports both de novo workflow generation and refinement of existing ones. Empirical results across seven benchmarks demonstrate that LAWA significantly reduces makespan while achieving competitive task performance, supporting efficient reuse of multi-agent workflows for recurrent queries.

items.title: Optimizing Readiness of Web-Based SIM-EPK (Health Research Ethics Management Information System) at The BHM (Bhakti Husada Mulia) Ethics Committee
items.abstract: This study explores the readiness of the ethics committee at Bhakti Husada Mulia Institute to transition from manual to web-based archive management using the SIM-EPK system. The research aims to assess the preparedness of committee administrators and reviewers in adapting to digital document management. To assess the readiness of human resources (administrators and reviewers) within the ethics committee at Bhakti Husada Mulia Institute in transitioning from a manual to a web-based system for managing research protocol document archives using SIM-EPK. Using a quantitative method with a pretest – posttest design, data were collected from all 24 committee members via an online questionnaire. The findings indicate a strong preference for web-based systems: 91.66% chose digital protocol management, 83.33% found it more flexible for completing ethics protocols, and 100% agreed that web-based systems ease access and retrieval of documents. However, despite these advantages, the web-based process sometimes took longer than manual procedures. This study concludes that digital adoption is promising, although further improvements are needed to streamline operations and ensure full integration. These results can serve as a model for other institutions undergoing digital transformation in research ethics administration. The ethics committee at BHM shows a high level of readiness for digital transformation using SIM-EPK. Web-based systems offer clear benefits in accessibility and document control, though technical and human factors still cause delays. Continued improvements and scaling strategies are needed to fully optimize digital ethics management across institutions.

items.title: Outcomes-Based Independent Learning Paradigm (OBILP): Effects on Students' Engagement and Performance in Chemistry
items.abstract: This study investigated the effects of the Outcomes-Based Independent Learning Paradigm (OBILP) on Grade 10 students’ engagement and performance in chemistry, focusing on the domains of gas laws, biomolecules, and chemical equations and reactions. An Explanatory Sequential Mixed-Methods design was employed. The quantitative phase utilized a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design involving Grade 10 students from Bacayawan National High School during the school year 2022–2023. Results indicated that both control and experimental groups exhibited very high levels of affective engagement and high levels of behavioral and cognitive engagement, with no significant differences across the three components. However, the experimental group achieved significantly higher mean scores (p = 0.010) and mean gain scores (p = 0.035) than the control group. No significant correlation was found between students’ engagement and performance before and after the intervention. The qualitative phase, through interviews and student journal entries, provided explanatory insights into these findings, revealing that OBILP enhanced student engagement and performance, while chemical reactions and equations remained the most challenging topic domain. These results suggest that OBILP has the potential to improve chemistry learning outcomes, although future studies should employ larger samples and broader contexts to strengthen generalizability.

items.title: PAG-Agent: Zero-Shot Personalized Music Album Generation via Aesthetic Profile Distillation
items.abstract: Large Music Models (LMMs) can synthesize high-fidelity audio and support increasingly flexible prompt control, yet modeling the subjective preferences of an individual listener remains underexplored. We present PAG-Agent, a zero-shot multimodal framework that uses an explicit Personal Aesthetic Profile to bridge user preference inference and music generation control. A multimodal LLM distills favorite-song audio and contextual user information into this structured representation, which a planning LLM translates into generation instructions for existing music synthesizers. We further introduce PA-Eval, which evaluates personalization through the Aesthetic Consistency Score (ACS) for target-user alignment and the Aesthetic Specificity Index (ASI) for cross-user specificity. Experiments with Personal-100 on multiple MLLM and music-generation backbones show consistent improvements over generic and direct conditioning. A 50-participant follow-up study further shows a correlation $r=0.64$ between ACS and subjective preference.

items.title: PandemIQ system in Poland: The hybrid approach to early detection of pandemic waves using interpretable AI models and GIS-based operational dashboards (ArcGIS)
items.abstract: Humans live surrounded by a variety of threats. These threats can be diverse: natural, chemical, technological, psychological, social, ecological, global, biological, and health-related. The latter, namely biological and health threats, are the most pressing and dangerous from a human perspective as they affect living organisms’ health. Examples include infectious diseases caused by viruses, bacteria, or parasites (e.g., influenza, COVID-19, Lyme disease). In Poland, epidemic cases of the acute infectious respiratory disease COVID-19, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, were first reported on March 4, 2020. The pandemic lasted three years. This scientific article attempts to present the architecture and functionality of the PandemIQ system. The system was designed for the early detection and forecasting of the regional risk of pandemic waves. The system is based on a hybrid artificial intelligence model that combines predictions based on epidemiological, mobility, and transportation data with interpretability (attention) mechanisms enabling visualization and decision justification. This paper provides a detailed discussion of the structure of decision reports for authorities, GIS-based operational dashboards (ArcGIS), and alternative solutions using the Apache ECharts library. It also presents validation procedures, data security aspects, and compliance with legal regulations (GDPR, AI Act). Simulation results using historical data on the spread of the SARS-CoV-2 virus indicate that the system can detect waves on average 7–14 days earlier than traditional epidemiological methods can, while maintaining a low false alarm rate.

items.title: Parallel science and technology for C2 in the agentic age: from military operations to peaceful sustainability and resiliency
items.abstract: Abstract Command and control (C2) has traditionally been framed as a military problem of sensing, deciding, coordinating, and acting under uncertainty, conflict, and time pressure. In the agentic age, however, this problem is being extended far beyond the battlefield, as human organizations become increasingly embedded in hybrid environments composed of artificial agents, digital twins, social sensing networks, foundation models, autonomous platforms, and cyber–physical–social institutions. This article develops a conceptual framework for parallel science and technology for C2 by revisiting the historical mission of C2 as a quest for certainty under diversity, uncertainty, and complexity (DUC), and by tracing its transformation toward focus, agility, and convergence (FAC). Building on parallel systems, artificial societies, computational experiments, parallel execution (ACP), cyber–physical–social systems (CPSS), C2 management (C2M), planning–readiness–execution–assessment (PREA) loops, social cognition operations, and parallel battlefield intelligence, the article argues that C2 should be reframed as a general science of coordinated adaptation. It further examines emerging agentic societies as a new operating ecology, explains why parallel science and technology are needed, and redefines the mission of future C2 around sustainability and resiliency. Rather than merely accelerating decision cycles or optimizing combat efficiency, parallel C2 aims to support anticipation, adaptation, trust, recovery, and responsible human agency across both military and civilian domains, thereby transforming command and control from post-hoc operational control into a science of sustainable and resilient coordination in the agentic age.

items.title: Partnering With Generative Artificial Intelligence for Quantitative Data Analysis in Nursing Research: A Practical Workflow for Ethical Collaboration
items.abstract: Reproducibility and replicability are our scientific and ethical mandate, and the foundation of trust in nursing science and research. Both rest on transparent documentation of how data were actually analyzed. The rising use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in research intersects with this mandate, with the potential to either support or undermine it, yet practical guidance for conducting GenAI-assisted quantitative analysis remains limited. This gap is particularly relevant for nurse scientists, who increasingly work with complex, biologically-informed datasets spanning genomics, symptoms, and patient outcomes. To address this gap, we present a practice-based guide for partnering with GenAI in quantitative data analysis in nursing research, grounded in a nursing-focused genomic research example. We cover GenAI literacy spanning three dimensions (technical, practical, and ethical) and a two-phase workflow for human-GenAI collaboration spanning planning and pre-specification through code development, formal analysis, translation, and human review and disclosure of GenAI use. The core principle is using GenAI as a tool, not a decision-maker, as scientific integrity requires that humans retain interpretive authority. We further propose a synthetic-data-first approach as a privacy safeguard. We illustrate these concepts through a genetics example, though the principles and workflow generalize to many quantitative nursing research contexts.

items.title: PAT: A Personality-Driven Augmentation and Transfer Learning Framework for Depression Detection on Social Media
items.abstract: Depression is a prevalent mental disorder that affects millions worldwide, with early detection crucial for effective intervention. While exist?ing methods have achieved promising results in automated depression detection, they face two key limitations: (1) noise in post screening: symptom-based semantic screening is easily misled by superficial lexical patterns, thereby introducing false-positive posts; (2) weak op?timization of the post encoder: relying solely on coarse user-level supervision signals pre?vents models from capturing depressive cues within individual posts. To address these limita?tions, we propose PAT, a Personality-driven Augmentation and Transfer learning frame?work. In the first phase, PAT optimizes a post?level encoder via a fine-grained contrastive learning objective, utilizing LLM-based data augmentation driven by classic personality the?ories to alleviate data scarcity. In the second phase, the trained post-level scorer is deployed for high-quality post filtering, while its en?coder parameters are seamlessly transferred for user-level tasks. Extensive experiments demon?strate that PAT significantly outperforms exist?ing methods. Furthermore, PAT delivers multi?granular interpretability by tracing post-level mental-state trajectories and highlighting key symptoms, thereby offering reliable diagnostic evidence for clinical practice.

items.title: PawSense_AI Assistant
items.abstract: The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence in everyday applications has created opportunities to improve access to pet-care information and support pet owners in making informed decisions about animal health and well-being. This paper presents PawSense AI, an AI-powered pet-care assistance system designed to provide accessible, interactive, and personalized support to pet owners through a web-based platform. The proposed system integrates generative artificial intelligence, image-based pet assessment, voice interaction, and location-based veterinary search within a unified interface. Users can interact with the system through natural-language queries, upload pet images for preliminary AI-assisted observations, and access information about nearby veterinary facilities. The application incorporates user authentication and database-supported conversation management to maintain individual accounts and chat histories. Voice transcription and multilingual response options further aim to improve accessibility and ease of interaction. The system is developed using Python and the Flask web framework, with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the user interface, database technologies for information management, and external AI and mapping services for intelligent responses and location-based information. PawSense AI is intended to complement existing pet-care resources by providing convenient access to general guidance and helping users identify relevant veterinary services. However, AI-generated observations are not a substitute for professional veterinary diagnosis, and the reliability of the system depends on the underlying AI models, external services, and input quality. The proposed platform demonstrates an integrated approach to AI-assisted pet-care information access, with potential for further development through systematic evaluation, improved personalization, and expanded multilingual capabilities. Keywords— PawSense AI, Artificial Intelligence, Pet Care, Generative AI, Image Analysis, Voice Assistant, Veterinary Services, Flask Web Application.

items.title: Paying for Nutrition: A Mechanism-Design Approach to the Nutrient Density Standard
items.abstract: Can a voluntary farm-gate payment improve the nutritional quality of food crops at a defensible cost? This paper proposes a Nutrient Density Bonus for verified protein, zinc, and iron in harvested wheat, alongside existing income protection. It compares three payment architectures: direct lot assays, contracts for specified practices, and evidence-backed claims subject to independent audits. A capped, volume-adjusted payment rule makes the unit of reward explicit; a simplified deterrence condition identifies the recovery and enforcement assumptions behind the audit mechanism. The proposed evaluation begins with a measurement season in western Kansas and northern Oklahoma, followed, only if feasible, by a controlled comparison over multiple harvests. Reference assays remain the basis for mineral verification unless predictive methods meet prespecified payment-relevant error tolerances. The policy must demonstrate additional crop-quality improvement, affordable verification, fair access, and acceptable effects on yield, income, food safety, and the environment. Higher grain mineral concentration is distinguished from nutrient output, bioavailability, and health benefit. The contribution is a policy-design framework and prospective evaluation plan; no pilot results or national cost estimate are reported. Status: Policy working paper, version 1.0; not peer reviewed. No new dataset, completed pilot, or national cost estimate is reported. Provenance: A revised archival adaptation of the June 2026 web proposal.
